definitions.explanation: Fireworks that are launched into the sky and explode at height, as opposed to handheld fireworks. A central feature of Japanese summer festivals.

examples.japanese: {打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび}がきれいだった。
{夏|なつ}は{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび}を{見|み}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: In summer, I go to see fireworks displays.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい}では{一万発|いちまんぱつ}の{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび}が{予定|よてい}されている。
examples.english: Ten thousand aerial fireworks are planned for this year's fireworks festival.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan's summer {花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい} (fireworks festivals) are major events attended by millions. Viewers wear {浴衣|ゆかた} and bring picnic blankets. Contrasts with {手持|てもち}ち{花火|はなび} (handheld sparklers), which are enjoyed in smaller, private settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび}を{見|み}る: to watch fireworks
- {打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび}が{上|あ}がる: fireworks go up
- {花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい}: fireworks festival
